ACMM (East) in CC No. 4277/2018 titled as Kaman Kumar Vaid Vs Umashankar Sharma & Anr., whereby the Ld. ACMM issued summons to the petitioners for the offence punishable u/s 452/380/34 & 120-B IPC.

sentences.text: It is alleged that the alleged persons as mentioned in the complaint committed offence punishable under section 452/354/380/120-B/506/34 IPC in respect of the said house and members of the family of the complainant on 15.05.2002.
It was also stated that an FIR bearing no. 135/2002 had been lodged by the said alleged persons at PS Trilok Puri for offences u/s 447/448/506/34 IPC.
A report was called from the police by the Ld.M.M. and during pre-summoning inquiry, the complainant examined six witnesses.
3) It is stated that respondent no. 2 and his father and brother had told petitioner no. 1 and one Kiran Pal that Sahdev Raj Vaid, father of the respondent no. 2, was the owner of several shops.
They showed to the petitioner no. 1 and Kiran Pal one shop each (Pvt. No. 2 & 3), both shops part of property no. B-17, Acharya Niketan, Mayur Vihar, Phase-1, Delhi-92.

Believing CR No. 116/2020 Page 2 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi them, petitioner no. 1 paid Rs. 12,000/- to them as advance/security for one shop and Kiran Pal paid a sum of Rs. 15,000/- as advance rent/security for one shop.

On 10.04.2002 they took petitioner no. 1 and Kiran Pal to the Registrar Office at Geeta Colony and Sahdev Raj Vaid executed Rent Deed in favour of the petitioner no. 1 in respect of shop no. 2 and Rent Deed in favour of Kiran Pal in respect of shop no. 3.
These rent deeds were got notarized by them from a Notary Public, who was also present there.
On the same date i.e. on 10.04.2002, they took petitioner no. 1 and Kiran Pal to those shops where repairs/renovation work was going on.
Upon reaching there, they started beating the labourers working there and forced them to leave the property.
In the meantime Umashankar reached there and he questioned those persons as to why they were beating his labourers in the property owned by his wife Smt. Sushma Sharma.

In the mean time police reached the spot and called both Umashankar and Sahdev Raj Vaid, father of the respondent no. 2, to show their respective documents regarding the property No.
B-17, Acharya Niketan.
Thereafter Umashankar locked his property B-17, Acharya Niketan and left from there.
Subsequently, on 11.04.2002 also Umashankar was beaten by respondent no. 2, his brother Ramankant Vaid and father Sehdev Raj Vaid.
In respect of the incident of 10.04.2002 and 11.04.2002 FIR No. 135/02, mentioned hereinabove, was got registered by Umashankar at PS Trilok Puri.
4) It is urged by ld.

Counsel for the petitioners that FIR No. 135/02, PS Pandav Nagar, is concerning the property in CR No. 116/2020 Page 3 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi issue and it has been registered against respondent no. 2, his father Shahdev Raj Vaid, and brother Ramankant Vaid.

It is stated that on 11.04.2002 respondent no. 2 and his father (now deceased) and brother tried to grab the property from Umashankar and Smt. Sushma Sharma and they also committed forgery and cheating by fabrication of false rent agreements with them in respect of the property in issue.
On that account on 11.04.2002 FIR No. 135/02 PS Trilok Puri was registered and charges were framed against respondent no. 2 and his brother u/s 451/323/356/34 & 420/468/471 r/w Section 120B IPC.
The said matter is at the stage of prosecution evidence, hence, there was no possibility of commission of the offence as alleged by the respondents in respect of the said property.
The present complaint has been filed as a counter blast to FIR No. 135/2002, PS Trilokpuri.
It is argued that none of the abovesaid facts have been considered by the Ld. A.C.M.M. while passing the impugned order dated 29.01.2020.

It is urged that the impugned order dated 29.01.2020 is in teeth of the order dated 20.08.2018 passed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court wherein the Hon'ble High Court had directed ) Shiv Charan @ Billu vs ) State (Nct Of Delhi) on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148862782/
2 the concerned M.M. to take into account to pass the order of summoning only after hearing the complainant and perusal of the material available on record.

sentences.text: It is urged that the ld. M.M. has passed the impugned order without taking into consideration the other material available on record and has also relied upon the statements of the witnesses examined by the complainant before passing the summoning order.
It is accordingly prayed that the impugned order dated 29.01.2020 may be set aside.
CR No. 116/2020 Page 4 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi 5)

On the other hand, it is contended by ld. Counsel for the respondent no. 2 that para 17 of the order of the Hon'ble High Court implies that the observations made therein by the Hon'ble High Court were suggestive in nature and not in the nature of directions to the Trial Court.
It is stated that directions cannot be given to the Trial Court to decide the issue of passing a summoning order u/s 204 Cr.P.C., which power solely vests with the Trial Court.

It is stated that from the facts and circumstances of the present case, prima facie a case is made out against the petitioners and hence,
taking of cognizance by the Ld. M.M. cannot be interfered with.
It is stated that it is not the condition precedent to issue process that the court necessarily must hold an enquiry as envisaged u/s 202 Cr.P.C. or direct investigation.
It is accordingly prayed that there is no infirmity in the order passed by the Ld. M.M. and the revision petition is liable to be dismissed.
6) The present complaint case was filed on 17.05.2002 u/s 200 Cr.P.C.
Vide the order dated 05.06.2002, the application of the complainant u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. was dismissed and an enquiry was conducted u/s 200 Cr.P.C.
Thereafter, vide order dated 08.05.2006 the complaint was dismissed.

Revision petition was filed before the court of Ld. ASJ and on 17.07.2006, the Ld. ASJ set aside the dismissal order and the matter was remanded back with the following observations:-
"Hence, the order dated 8.5.2006 is hereby set aside whereby the complaint has been dismissed and ld. Magistrate is directed to proceed to take the prima CR No.
116/2020 Page 5 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi facie view of the matter and filing of the status report or the finding of the witnesses being interested or the finding that the complainant was not having any prima facie proof of ownership should not be given any consideration at this stage."
7) The matter was accordingly remanded back to Ld. MM and thereafter the complaint was again dismissed by the Ld. MM vide order dated 07.05.2008.
A revision petition was filed assailing the said order dated 07.05.2008 and the same was disposed off by the order dated 25.03.2009 passed by Ld. ASJ and it was observed as follows:-
"So long as the principle of correctness is concerned, the impugned order dated 07.05.08, the directions of ld. ASJ has been fully complied with by ld.

MM therefore,
it also meet out the standard of correctness and legality as well.
I have also perused the statement of CW 2 Kanchan Lata who happens the sister of revisionist and in her statement some elements of criminality has come on record.

Statement of this witness appears to have been overlooked by the court of original jurisdiction which ) Shiv Charan @ Billu vs ) State (Nct Of Delhi) on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148862782/
3 goes to the root of the case for the just decision of dismissal or issuing of process qua accused persons.

sentences.text: However, in the pursuit of objective of justice, to ensure the legal certainty and legitimate expectations the impugned order 7.5.08 is set aside and the case is remanded back to the court of ld. ACMM/MM concerned with the direction to pass a fresh order on the issue of process after considering the statement of CW2 Kanchan Lata along with other collateral facts on record and complying the directions passed by the then ld. ASJ order dated 17.7.06."

8) Pursuant thereto, vide order dated 04.06.2010, the complaint was again dismissed by the Ld.
MM.

The said order was assailed before the Ld. ASJ and vide order dated 21.03.2015, the revision petition was allowed and the order dated 04.06.2010 of the Ld. MM was set aside and the Ld. ASJ directed the parties CR No. 116/2020 Page 6 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi to appear before Ld. Trial Court and thereby summoning the petitioners as accused.

The said order dated 21.03.2015 was challenged before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court vide Crl. M.C. no. 1452 of 2015 and Crl. M.A. 5348 of 2015 vide which the Hon'ble Delhi High Court set aside the impugned order dated 21.03.2015 and made the following observations in para 10, 11 and 12 of the order dated 20.08.2018:-
"10. ....... The criminal complaint as indeed the status reports submitted by the police at the time of initial inquiry and inquiry directed by order dated 27.10.2007 have brought to the fore certain additional facts including what is referred to by the petitioners as 'admissions' in the pleadings and proceedings of the civil suit.
11.

It may be added here that there is material presented to show investigation into FIR No. 135/2002 registered at the instance of the petitioners was completed in due course and charge-sheet was laid in the court of Metropolitan Magistrate on which the complainant of the case at hand along with one another (Raman) have been summoned.

It further appears on 21.12.2009 the Metropolitan Magistrate took the said case, inter alia, against the complainant to trial by directing charge to be framed for offences punishable under sections 420/468/471 read with Section 120-B IPC and under Sections 451, 323, 356 read with Sections 34 IPC.
12.
If the summoning order were to be passed only on the basis of scrutiny of the testimony of six witnesses presented by the complainant it would lead to a one-sided view to be taken.
That is not the object of preliminary inquiry.

This is why the law confers on the court of Magistrate, the jurisdiction to "postpone" the question of issuance of process and undertake further probe in terms of Section 202 Cr.P.C."
9) The Hon'ble Delhi High Court made further observations in para 16 and 17 which are as follows:-
"16.
The proceedings, in the considered view of this CR No. 116/2020 Page 7 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi Court, stood vitiated by order dated 27.10.2007 of the court of magistrate.
Opting to call upon the police "to make an enquiry" was not permissible in law.
In terms of Section 202 Cr.P.C. a direction to the police could be given to not to "enquire" but "to investigate".

The investigation by the police would entail the ) Shiv Charan @ Billu vs ) State (Nct Of Delhi) on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148862782/
4 procedure governed by Chapter XII of Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Shiv Charan @ Billu vs ) State (Nct Of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No investigation in that sense of the matter has either been ordered or secured by the Metropolitan Magistrate till date.

The order dated 27.10.2007 directing an "enquiry" being impermissible in law, the report received in its wake could also not have been acted upon.
17.
The needful correction in the course must be done now.
The impugned orders are set aside.

The question as to whether there is need for further "inquiry" by court or "investigation by police" under Section 202 Cr.P.C. is kept open for a call thereupon to be taken by the concerned Metropolitan Magistrate, after hearing the complainant and perusal of available material."
10) The petition filed before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court was disposed off with the above directions.

Accordingly, the concerned Metropolitan Magistrate was to take a call on the issue as to whether there was a need for further "Inquiry" by court or "Investigation by Police" u/s 202 Cr.P.C.
after hearing the complainant and perusal of available material.

The abovesaid said observations of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court made in para 17 have to be read in context of the observations made in para 10, 11 and 12 of its order dated 20.08.2018, as reproduced hereinabove.

11) Perusal of the impugned order dated 29.01.2020 reveals that the Ld. MM has issued summons to accused Umashankar, Sushma Sharma, Shiv Charan @ Billu, Ishwar and Kiran Pal for offences punishable u/s 452/380/34 and section 120-B IPC.

While issuing the summons, the Ld. MM referred to CR No. 116/2020 Page 8 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi and discussed the pre-summoning evidence of CW-1, CW-2, CW-3, CW-4, CW-5, CW-6 and observed that since all the alleged persons were residents of Delhi, no further inquiry was required to be conducted by the court to decide the issue of process.

The Ld. MM further discussed the pre-summoning evidence of the witnesses and held that the material on record was sufficient to prima facie show that the offences punishable u/s 452/380/34 and section 120-B IPC were committed by the alleged persons.

It may however, be noted that the Ld. MM in the impugned order dated 29.01.2020, has relied upon the pre- summoning evidence of the six witnesses and did not take into consideration other available material on record as observed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in its order dated 20.08.2018.

Though, the Ld. MM has mentioned in the impugned order that he had heard the complainant and also considered the material available on record, however, there is no mention whatsoever at all as to what material was considered and the impugned order is entirely based upon the pre-summoning evidence of the witnesses and hence, not in consonance with the intent and purport of the order dated 20.08.2018 passed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court.
12) In view of the aforesaid discussions, the impugned order dated 29.01.2020 passed by the Ld.
MM is set aside.
The revision petition is accordingly allowed.

13) Parties are directed to appear before the Ld. M.M., who shall proceed with the matter as per law and complying with CR No. 116/2020 Page 9 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi the order dated 20.08.2018 passed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court.
14) TCR be sent back alongwith copy of this judgment.
